label: GO WITH CONDITIONS
call: Sell medical delivery to health systems as a done-for-you service priced per run, and subcontract every flight to a certified operator already approved for the corridor. Buy no aircraft, and drop the retail and food lean.

why.point: Retail and food drops cost $15 to $25 against $8 to $12 needed, and the giants already own the merchants.
No one pays for a software middle layer; operators build their own dispatch.
Approval takes 12 to 24 months; subcontracting an approved operator skips the wait.
Health systems pay for the sample arriving, worth about nine times a software seat.

minority.quote: if the contacts turn out to be in retail, the merchant aggregator goes back on the table. It should not default to E.
minority.would_have_to_be_true: Contacts are in retail, Wing or Zipline grants partner access in 60 days, and 5 merchants commit to $10+ a drop.

next_steps.action: 10 calls with hospital lab and pharmacy logistics heads, 5 with certified operators.
Operator subcontract signed at $25 or less per run, with indemnity.
Two paid pilots signed; dispatch the first runs by hand.

kill_criteria: No operator subcontract by 2026-12-29 or no paid pilot by 2027-01-28: stop, keep the cash, and reconvene.
conditions: By 2026-11-29: 10 healthcare contacts who pay to move an item today; price a ground courier buy under $300k
By 2026-12-29: Part 135 operator subcontract at $25 or less per run, with indemnity and insurance
By 2027-01-28: two paid pilots, $2,000 monthly minimum, 20+ runs a week, operator cost at or under 60% of price
Own chain-of-custody liability policy before the first paid run
First pilot's 30-day cash above 2x cost to win and serve before signing hospital two
By 2027-04-30: positive gross margin and runs per week growing weekly
At 2027-10-30: no customer above 40% of revenue
No lease, hire, or spend above $100k until the subcontract and pilots clear

fights.crux: Will anyone pay for a software layer?
fights.story: Round 1 was unanimous for software. Bezos and Buffett argued no buyer exists and convinced themselves; Graham, Hormozi and Elon followed.
Hormozi and Elon argued the managed service; four seats moved from software to selling the delivery.

fights.crux: What if the contacts are in retail?
fights.story: Graham and Codie backed a retail merchant tool; Hormozi, Buffett and Elon said retail contacts mean wait. Unresolved.

amendments.amendment: Replace the fixed $50 floor with the 60% cost ratio.
amendments.reason: Hormozi's 30-day cash test now guards the economics.

amendments.amendment: Runs per week must grow weekly by month 6.
30-day pilot cash above 2x cost to win and serve before hospital two.
Own liability policy plus operator indemnity before the first run.
amendments.reason: Three other seats raised the same liability risk.

amendments.amendment: At least 20 runs a week per pilot, reviewed weekly.
Price out buying a ground medical courier by day 30.
Retail contacts reopen the merchant aggregator instead of waiting.
amendments.reason: Three seats showed retail drops lose money; minority report.

cheapest_test: Before writing code, one health system signs a paid pilot letter and one operator quotes $25 or less a run in writing.
revisit: 2027-01-28 with signed pilots, run price, operator cost and runs per week; sooner if the contacts are in retail.
